LAKEWOOD, Colo.


, Nov. 19, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / -- Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, Inc. (NYSE: NGVC) today announced results for its fourth quarter and fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 and provided its outlook for fiscal 2027.


**Highlights for Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Compared to Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2025**


- Net sales increased 3.4% to $347.5 million;
- Daily average comparable store sales increased 2.5%, and 6.7% on a two-year basis;
- Net income was $11.3 million, with diluted earnings per share of $0.48; and
- Opened three new stores.


**Highlights for Fiscal 2026 Compared to Fiscal 2025**


- Net sales increased 1.8% to $1.36 billion;
- Daily average comparable store sales increased 1.5%, and increased 8.8% on a two-year basis;
- 23rd consecutive year of positive comparable store sales growth;
- Net income increased 1.5% to $47.1 million, with diluted earnings per share of $2.03;
- Adjusted EBITDA increased 0.5% to $98.4 million; and
- Opened seven new stores and relocated/remodeled two stores.


"In fiscal 2026, we delivered our 23rd consecutive year of positive comparable store sales growth, a record sustained across many economic cycles that reflects the durability of our differentiated model. We finished the year with momentum, as daily average comparable store sales growth increased sequentially in each of the last two quarters, reaching 2.5% in the fourth quarter. We are pleased with these results given the challenging retail environment," said Kemper Isely, Co-President. "Fiscal 2026 marked the first year of our strategy to accelerate our new store unit growth rate, during which we opened seven stores and entered our 22nd state. During the year, we also enhanced our e-commerce capabilities, providing customers with additional convenient ways to shop with us."


Mr. Isely continued, "We remain focused on consistently delivering high-quality natural and organic products, everyday value through our Always AffordableSM pricing strategy, and the convenience of our smaller-store format. With significant expansion opportunities in new and existing markets, a target of 4% to 5% annual unit growth and enduring consumer demand for health and wellness, we believe we are well positioned to drive long-term growth and value for our stockholders."


In addition to presenting the financial results of Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, Inc. and its subsidiaries (collectively, the Company) in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), the Company is also presenting EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, which are non-GAAP financial measures. The reconciliation from GAAP to these non-GAAP financial measures is provided at the end of this earnings release.


**Operating Results — Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2026 Compared to Fourth Quarter Fiscal 2025**


Net sales during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 increased $11.4 million, or 3.4%, to $347.5 million compared to the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, due to a $4.6 million increase in comparable store sales and an $8.0 million increase in new store sales, partially offset by a $1.2 million decrease in net sales related to closed stores. Daily average comparable store sales increased 2.5% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, comprised of a 3.1% increase in daily average transaction size and a 0.5% decrease in daily average transaction count.


Gross profit during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 increased $2.6 million, or 2.7%, to $101.7 million compared to $99.0 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. Gross profit reflects earnings after product and store occupancy costs. Gross margin during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was 29.2% compared to 29.5% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. The decrease in gross margin of 21 basis points was driven by lower product margin primarily due to higher merchandise inventory shrink and freight costs, partially offset by store occupancy cost leverage.


Store expenses during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 increased 2.8% to $74.5 million. Store expenses as a percentage of net sales during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 were 21.4% compared to 21.6% during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by expense management.


Administrative expenses during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 increased 3.7% to $11.3 million. Administrative expenses as a percentage of net sales were 3.2% for each of the fourth quarters of fiscal 2026 and 2025.


Pre-opening expenses during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 were $0.7 million compared to $0.2 million during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.


Operating income for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $15.2 million compared to $15.5 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. Operating margin for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was 4.4% compared to 4.6% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.


Net income for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $11.3 million, or $0.48 diluted earnings per share, compared to net income of $11.8 million, or $0.51 diluted earnings per share, for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.


Adjusted EBITDA for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $24.9 million compared to $24.4 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025.


**Operating Results — Fiscal 2026 Compared to Fiscal 2025**


Net sales during fiscal 2026 increased $24.4 million, or 1.8%, to $1.36 billion compared to fiscal 2025, due to a $16.0 million increase in comparable store sales and a $14.6 million increase in new store sales, partially offset by a $6.2 million decrease in net sales related to closed stores. Daily average comparable store sales increased 1.5% in fiscal 2026, comprised of a 2.1% increase in daily average transaction size and a 0.6% decrease in daily average transaction count.


Gross profit during fiscal 2026 increased $3.1 million, or 0.8%, to $401.0 million compared to $397.9 million in fiscal 2025. Gross profit reflects earnings after product and store occupancy costs. Gross margin decreased to 29.6% during fiscal 2026 compared to 29.9% in fiscal 2025. The decrease in gross margin of 31 basis points was driven by lower product margin primarily due to higher merchandise inventory shrink.


Store expenses during fiscal 2026 increased 0.3% to $291.3 million. Store expenses as a percentage of net sales during fiscal 2026 were 21.5% compared to 21.8% during fiscal 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by expense management.


Administrative expenses during fiscal 2026 decreased 1.4% to $43.7 million, primarily driven by the business interruption insurance recovery gain of $2.0 million and lower compensation expenses, partially offset by higher technology expenses. Administrative expenses as a percentage of net sales were 3.2% during fiscal 2026 compared to 3.3% in fiscal 2025.


Pre-opening expenses during fiscal 2026 were $3.0 million compared to $1.0 million during fiscal 2025.


Operating income for fiscal 2026 was $62.9 million compared to $62.0 million in fiscal 2025. Operating margin for fiscal 2026 was 4.6% compared to 4.7% in fiscal 2025.


Net income for fiscal 2026 was $47.1 million, or $2.03 diluted earnings per share, compared to net income of $46.4 million, or $2.00 diluted earnings per share, for fiscal 2025.


Adjusted EBITDA for fiscal 2026 was $98.4 million compared to $97.9 million in fiscal 2025.


**Balance Sheet and Cash Flow**


As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $32.1 million in cash and cash equivalents and no outstanding borrowings on its $70.0 million revolving credit facility.


During fiscal 2026, the Company generated $87.4 million in cash from operations and invested $53.5 million in net capital expenditures, primarily for new and relocated/remodeled stores and real property acquisitions.


**Dividend Announcement**


Today, the Company announced the declaration of a quarterly cash dividend of $0.15 per common share. The dividend will be paid on December 9, 2026, to stockholders of record at the close of business on November 30, 2026.


**Growth and Development**


During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the Company opened three new stores. The Company ended the fourth quarter with 175 stores in 22 states. During fiscal 2026 the Company opened seven new stores.

**About Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage**


Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, Inc. (NYSE: NGVC) is an expanding specialty retailer of natural and organic groceries, body care products and dietary supplements. The grocery products sold by Natural Grocers must meet strict quality guidelines and may not contain artificial flavors, preservatives, or sweeteners (as defined in its standards), synthetic colors, or partially hydrogenated or hydrogenated oils. The Company sells only USDA certified organic produce and exclusively pasture-raised, non-confinement dairy products, and free-range eggs. Natural Grocers' flexible smaller-store format allows it to offer affordable prices in a shopper-friendly, clean and convenient retail environment. The Company also provides extensive free science-based nutrition education programs to help customers make informed health and nutrition choices. The Company, founded in 1955, has 175 stores in 22 states.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


**(Unaudited)**


*EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA*


EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are not measures of financial performance under GAAP. We define EBITDA as net income before interest expense, provision for income taxes, depreciation and amortization. We define Adjusted EBITDA as EBITDA as adjusted to exclude the effects of certain income and expense items that management believes make it more difficult to assess the Company's actual operating performance, including impairment charges, store closing costs, share-based compensation, amortization of software hosting arrangement (SaaS) implementation costs and business interruption insurance recovery gain.

EBITDA increased 0.8% to $23.7 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $23.5 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. EBITDA increased 2.2% to $95.9 million for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to $93.8 million for the year ended September 30, 2025. EBITDA as a percentage of net sales was 6.8% and 7.0% for the fourth quarter of 2026 and 2025, respectively. EBITDA as a percentage of net sales was 7.1% and 7.0% for the years ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.


Adjusted EBITDA increased 2.2% to $24.9 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $24.4 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025. Adjusted EBITDA increased 0.5% to $98.4 million for the year ended September 30, 2026 compared to $97.9 million for the year ended September 30, 2025. Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of net sales was 7.2% and 7.3% for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and 2025, respectively. Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of net sales was 7.3% and 7.4% for the years ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.


Management believes some investors' understanding of our performance is enhanced by including EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, which are non-GAAP financial measures. We believe EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA provide additional information about: (i) our operating performance, because they assist us in comparing the operating performance of our stores on a consistent basis, as they remove the impact of non-cash depreciation and amortization expense as well as items not directly resulting from our core operations, such as interest expense and income taxes and (ii) our performance and the effectiveness of our operational strategies. Additionally, EBITDA is a component of a measure in our financial covenants under our credit facility.


Furthermore, management believes some investors use EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA as supplemental measures to evaluate the overall operating performance of companies in our industry. Management believes that some investors' understanding of our performance is enhanced by including these non-GAAP financial measures as a reasonable basis for comparing our ongoing results of operations. By providing these non-GAAP financial measures, together with a reconciliation from net income, we believe we are enhancing investors' understanding of our business and our results of operations, as well as assisting investors in evaluating how well we are executing our strategic initiatives.


Our competitors may define EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA differently, and as a result, our measures of EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA may not be directly comparable to EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA of other companies. Items excluded from EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are significant components in understanding and assessing financial performance. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are supplemental measures of operating performance that do not represent and should not be considered in isolation or as an alternative to, or substitute for, net income or other financial statement data presented in the consolidated financial statements as indicators of financial performance. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA have limitations as analytical tools, and should not be considered in isolation, or as a substitute for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Some of the limitations are:


- EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect our cash expenditures, or future requirements for capital expenditures or contractual commitments;


- EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, our working capital needs;


- EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect any depreciation or interest expense for leases classified as finance leases;


- EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect the interest expense, or the cash requirements necessary to service interest or principal payments on our debt;


- Adjusted EBITDA does not reflect share-based compensation, impairment of long-lived assets, store closing costs, amortization of SaaS implementation costs and business interruption insurance recovery gain;


- EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect our tax expense or the cash requirements to pay our taxes; and


- Although depreciation and amortization are non-cash charges, the assets being depreciated and amortized will often have to be replaced in the future and EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA do not reflect any cash requirements for such replacements.


Due to these limitations, EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as measures of discretionary cash available to us to invest in the growth of our business. We compensate for these limitations by relying primarily on our GAAP results and using EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA as supplemental information.
